title: 9-slice `DPITexture` used in `StyleBoxTexture` stretches in a wrong way when window size is changed unless it's been rendered at least once at native oversampling (`canvas_items` stretch mode)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.5.1.stable.official [f62fdbde1]

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable - Manjaro Linux `#1` SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu, 18 Dec 2025 13:46:28 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 7600 (RADV NAVI33) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 15.54 GiB memory

### Issue description

In my game, most UI styleboxes are `StyleBoxTexture`s with a `DPITexture`. I noticed that when my game starts up and restores the window size and position from settings, the styleboxes that aren't present on the first scene that's run stretch wrong. Once the window is resized such that the oversampling factor is `1.0` and the texture has been "seen", it will stretch correctly whenever the window is resized.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set `display/window/stretch/mode` to `canvas_items` (aspect does not seem to matter)
2. Add a control that renders at least two different styleboxes depending on state
3. Create two `StyleBoxTexture`s for each state, each using a `DPITexture` with texture margins
4. Run the project, maximize it or resize it and do something to render the other state of the control, notice the wrong scaling

For the MRP: The svg's are made so that they are the same boxes with inverted colors. Run the project, maximize it or resize it and hover the button. Unmaximize the window and hover the button again. Maximize it again and hover the button. The stylebox will now stretch correctly.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[dpitexture-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24569421/dpitexture-bug.zip)
